text: Found it — there's a typo in the prompt template, `{{custmerName}}` instead of `{{customerName}}`, so Handlebars renders it as an empty string and the model just sees "named ." with no actual name, producing a generic welcome message. I want to verify this by grepping the exact line to confirm the typo verbatim and check where else this prompt might be used.
The prompt template has `{{custmerName}}` while the input is `customerName`. I'll confirm the exact text and check how the template engine handles a missing variable.

text: I'm preparing to write answer.json containing the verbatim welcome-message line with the typo'd placeholder, and will check the file doesn't already exist before writing it.
The render now shows "Ada". Writing `answer.json` to the project root.

The bug was a typo in the greet prompt template: `{{custmerName}}` instead of `{{customerName}}`. Handlebars rendered it as blank, so the model never received the name and produced a generic welcome.

I fixed the placeholder in `prompts/greet.prompt`. Rendering the template with `customerName: 'Ada'` now gives "...welcome for the customer named Ada." I also wrote `answer.json` in the project root. I didn't touch `package.json` or add dependencies, and I did not run the Genkit flow end to end, since the CLAUDE.md asks me not to run Genkit commands myself.
